newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond subdued by holidays and expected U.S data.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond subdued by holidays and expected U.S data.

text.p: The primary market was quiet on Monday, due to public holidays in Asia and in anticipation of the release of a batch of U.S. data this week.
"This will remain a quiet week," a syndicate manager at a British bank said.
"It is a big week for holidays, mainly Japan's Golden Week, and possible volatility in U.S. Treasuries will make it hard to launch large issues," he said.

On Tuesday, the first quarter Employment Cost Index and April consumer confidence figures will be released. On Wednesday comes U.S. GDP for the first quarter, on Thursday, the April NAPM report and on Friday, the all-important employment report for April.
All will be closely watched for signs of a build-up of inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy.
A number of emerging market borrowers tapped the market on Monday, including Brazil with an innovative three-tranche parallel bond issue totalling around $540 million equivalent.
Bankers said the deal had found good institutional demand, but had failed to take the retail market by storm.

ING Barings, Banque Paribas and Creditanstanlt-Bankverein underwrote the bond, which carried a 6.625 percent coupon on each of the five-year tranches in Dutch guilders, Austrian schillings and French francs.
The bonds will redenominate into the euro when the single European currency is introduced, and the three tranches then become fungible, enhancing liquidity.
Dealers said Argentina and Mexico were also eyeing such a structure.
Mexico's Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) launched a long-awaited five-year dollar bond, increased to $300 million from a $250 milion launch size.
The deal was priced to yield 160 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, and lead manager SBC Warburg said there was strong demand out of Asia and the U.S.

In sterling, Morgan Stanley lead managed a 125 million stg 25-year bond for Autolink Concessionaires (M6) plc, which will be used to finance a 100 kilometre dual three-lane motorway providing the main non-rail land route between England and Scotland.
The deal, part of the government's private finance initiative, was guaranteed by the triple-A rated Financial Security Assurance.
